system.description:
Predating even Damascene steel, Blood Tempering has seen extensive use through the nights of the Crusades. Rather than envenom her blade, the Assamite imparts a measure of her own resilience into weapons or armor by bathing them in her vitae. Viziers use the power to preserve their oldest relics, and the clay tablets recording the clan's earliest history owe their survival to repeated Blood Tempering.

System: The character spends a Willpower Trait and coats the item with her blood — roughly one Blood Trait per foot of length for a weapon (an average sword needs three, a lance as many as 15), or three Blood Traits per extra soak die desired for armor. A treated weapon's damage is increased by one die and becomes unbreakable by anything short of a supernatural power of greater rating than the Assamite's Fortitude, or catastrophic mundane force. Treated armor gains an extra soak die and similar durability, though the wearer can still be harmed by force that passes through it. This power cannot be applied to flexible items such as whips, leather armor or silk robes.
system.source: Libellus Sanguinis III: Wolves at the Door, Book Two: Saracens
